title: Gain-cell NAND string with dual-gate bypassable read transistors
idea: [Box: storage-node gate | dual-gate IGZO 2T0C | series-string current sense | monolithic vertical string | Si | 3D-NAND hole-and-plate deposition] Build 2T0C gain cells along a vertical macaroni string like 3D NAND; each read transistor has a back word-plate that, driven high, forces it on regardless of its stored node, so unselected cells act as pass gates and only the selected cell's storage node modulates string current. Write transistors hang off a second vertical write-bitline in the same hole.
why: Attacks 'no manufacturable 3D cell' (fact 2) and the capacitor wall (fact 1): no capacitor at all, reuses 3D-NAND tier economics; 64-128 cells per hole could give ~5x bits per footprint vs 6F2 at F=12 nm.

title: Freestanding single-crystal SrTiO3 membranes bonded as planar DRAM capacitors
idea: [Box: paraelectric perovskite charge | Si 4F2 VCT | charge-share SA | low-temperature membrane bonding | SrTiO3 donor wafer | epitaxy + water-soluble Sr3Al2O6 release] Grow epitaxial SrRuO3/SrTiO3 at ~700 C on a donor, free it by dissolving a Sr3Al2O6 sacrificial layer, and bond the membrane onto the finished transistor array below 300 C, then pattern planar or <=10:1 capacitors with k~150-300. The crystal's thermal budget never touches the access transistor or lower tiers.
why: Capacitor charge wall (fact 1): k~150+ reaches 5 fF at AR<10 instead of 60-75:1, deleting the deepest etch; also makes a capacitor that can sit on any 3D tier.

title: Dedicated deep-trench capacitor wafer hybrid-bonded onto transistor wafer
idea: [Box: single-crystal Si trench charge | Si VCT | charge-share SA | wafer-on-wafer hybrid bond, one pad per storage node | low-grade Si capacitor wafer | Bosch DRIE + ALD] Etch capacitors as 100:1+ trenches into a separate Si wafer (single-crystal Si etches deeper and straighter than oxide molds, and the doped wafer itself is the plate), then bond it face-to-face to the access-transistor wafer using oversized self-aligned Cu pads per storage node.
why: Capacitor wall (fact 1) plus process decoupling: Cs >10 fF possible and the high-AR mold module leaves the transistor wafer, so each wafer runs on its own optimized line.

title: Vertical bitlines climb bonded array tiers to one shared sense amp
idea: [Box: 1T1C charge | buried-channel Si FET | sense amp multiplexed across tiers | 8-tier stack of array-only wafers | thinned Si | hybrid bond + sub-um through-tier vias] Stack 4-8 thinned array-only wafers (no periphery) on one periphery wafer and drop every bitline segment through through-tier vias to a sense amp time-shared among tiers, so sense amps and decoders are amortized over 8x the cells.
why: Periphery ~49% of die (fact 7): periphery share falls toward ~10%, ~1.6-1.8x bits per processed silicon area, and HBM-class capacity without per-die TSV keep-outs (fact 6).

title: Bond interface doubles as a shared bitline for mirrored arrays
idea: [Box: 1T1C charge | 4F2 VCT | differential cross-interface sensing | face-to-face mirror bond | Si | Cu-Cu hybrid bond] Two mirror-image VCT arrays are finished with bitline half-lines on top and bonded face-to-face so the Cu halves fuse into one bitline serving cells above and below; the sense amp compares a cell on one side with the idle half on the other, giving folded-bitline noise rejection in a 4F2 open layout.
why: Density at fixed F: two cell layers per bitline layer (2x bits per footprint), and differential sensing recovers margin lost when Cs is capped (fact 1).

title: Per-tier thin-film decoders replace 3D DRAM wordline staircases
idea: [Box: lateral 1T1C | IGZO lateral FET | conventional SA | monolithic 3D tiers | Si | same ALD IGZO forms a decoder in each tier] Build a tiny IGZO decoder at the array edge of every tier that listens to a shared vertical bundle of log2(N) tier-address lines plus one wordline-drive line, so N tiers need ~log2(N)+k vertical contacts instead of an N-step staircase.
why: 3D break-even at 26+ tiers (fact 2) is eroded by staircase area and trim-etch steps; removing the staircase saves ~5-10% die area and dozens of process steps at 64+ tiers.

title: Solid-electrolyte double-layer nanocapacitors as DRAM storage nodes
idea: [Box: electric-double-layer ionic charge | Si VCT | charge-share SA | BEOL over array | Si | ALD solid proton/Li-ion conductor between blocking electrodes] Replace the dielectric with an ultrathin solid electrolyte so charge sits in Helmholtz double layers (~20 uF/cm2, roughly 3x a 0.5 nm-EOT high-k), giving ~5 fF with only ~10:1 aspect ratio.
why: Capacitor wall (fact 1): ~3x capacitance per area, cutting capacitor AR ~6x; risks are ionic response time (<100 ns needed) and electronic leakage.

title: N-type-only IGZO sense latches built inside every 3D tier
idea: [Box: lateral 1T1C | IGZO access | nMOS-only bootstrapped dynamic latch | monolithic BEOL tiers | Si | ALD IGZO] Rather than hauling every tier's bitline down to CMOS under the array, build a compact n-only cross-coupled latch (precharge-evaluate with bootstrap capacitors) from the same IGZO in each tier, sensing short local bitlines and driving amplified full-swing data onto a global line.
why: Charge-share ratio (fact 1) and under-array periphery limits (fact 7): 4-8x shorter local bitlines let Cs fall to ~2 fF, removing the need for high-AR capacitors.

title: Carbon-nanotube forests as capacitor bottom electrodes on each pad
idea: [Box: MIM charge on CNT bundle | Si VCT | charge-share SA | BEOL | Si | self-aligned catalyst dot + ~450 C CVD + conformal ALD ZrO2/TiN] Grow a short vertically aligned CNT bundle from a catalyst dot plated selectively on each storage-node pad, then coat it conformally with high-k and a TiN plate; the forest gives 10-30x surface area per footprint at 1-2 um height with no mold etch.
why: Capacitor wall (fact 1): surface area replaces the aspect-ratio race and skips the 60-75:1 oxide mold etch.

title: Plate-less floating capacitor between complementary bitlines (2T1C)
idea: [Box: differential floating MIM | two lateral transistors | fully differential SA | lateral 3D tier | Si | ALD] Connect each end of a lateral 3D capacitor through its own access transistor to BL and BLB on opposite sides of the tier, with no common plate; data is the sign of the voltage across the capacitor, so a read gives twice the 1T1C signal from one capacitor and the plate layer disappears from every tier.
why: Capacitor wall (fact 1) and tier height (fact 2): 2x signal halves the required Cs, and dropping the plate cuts tier stack height ~15-20%.

title: Vertical CCD memory: charge buckets shifted down gate-stacked pillars
idea: [Box: charge packets in channel potential wells | no access transistor, clocked word-plates | floating-diffusion sense at pillar base | 3D-NAND-like plate stack | Si or IGZO channel | blanket plate deposition + one hole etch] Each tier plate is a CCD gate around a vertical channel; three-phase clocking shifts packets down to one sense node at the base and recirculates them to the top, turning each hole into a 64-128-bit rotating shift register.
why: No 3D cell (fact 2) and periphery (fact 7): no capacitor or transistor per bit and one sense node per hole; ~64 ns per 64-bit burst suits row-buffer-style access, ~3-5x DRAM density.

title: Dies stand edge-on on the base die, wired through cut edges
idea: [Box: standard 1T1C | Si FET | conventional SA | edge-mounted 'bookshelf' dies | thinned Si | dicing exposes top metal + edge micro-bump plating] Instead of stacking DRAM dies flat with TSVs, stand thinned dies vertically on the logic base die and bring thousands of fine wires out of the polished die edge, where top-metal lines exposed by dicing are plated into edge bumps.
why: HBM TSV tax (fact 6): no TSV keep-out area and no thinning/TSV yield loss (20-30%); capacity scales with dies per row rather than stack height.

title: Alternate tiers rotate wordline direction 90 degrees against row hammer
idea: [Box: lateral 1T1C | IGZO lateral FET | standard SA | monolithic 3D tiers | Si | ALD] In a stacked array, tier k runs wordlines along x and tier k+1 along y, so no wordline has a parallel aggressor directly above or below, and in-tier neighbors are separated by grounded shield lines from the same metal.
why: Row hammer (fact 9): vertical parallel coupling disappears, pushing flip thresholds back toward 10k-100k activations and freeing mitigation refresh bandwidth.

title: Gain cell split across tiers: IGZO write above, silicon read below
idea: [Box: storage-node gate | IGZO write FET + Si read FET | current sense | sequential BEOL over FEOL | Si | ALD IGZO over 28 nm CMOS] Put the ultra-low-leakage IGZO write transistor in a BEOL tier directly over a high-drive Si read transistor in the substrate, with the vertical via between them as the storage node, giving each cell IGZO retention and Si read current in ~4-6F2.
why: Refresh (fact 3) and capacitor wall (fact 1): retention >1 s, no capacitor, Si-speed read; refresh energy down ~10x.

title: Tall silicon pillar as inversion-layer capacitor, no MIM mold
idea: [Box: MOS inversion charge | VCT on the same pillar | charge-share SA | monolithic | single-crystal Si | deep Si pillar etch + ALD high-k/metal plate wrap] Extend each VCT pillar ~1 um downward and wrap the lower section with a high-k/metal plate at fixed bias, so electrons in the sidewall inversion layer form the cell capacitance (~4 fF for a 20 nm pillar at 0.5 nm EOT); single-crystal dark generation (~few e-/s) is negligible against ~25k stored electrons.
why: Capacitor wall (fact 1): one etched Si feature is both transistor and capacitor, replacing the 70:1 oxide mold + MIM module and cutting masks.

title: Layer-transferred 4H-SiC access transistors for hour-scale retention
idea: [Box: MIM charge | 4H-SiC MOSFET | charge-share SA | Smart Cut SiC film onto array wafer | reusable SiC donor | high-temperature activation before bonding] Transfer thin 4H-SiC films (3.26 eV gap, intrinsic carriers ~1e-9 cm^-3) from a reusable donor and build access transistors whose junction and GIDL leakage sit orders below Si, so cells refresh every minutes to hours.
why: Refresh (fact 3): recovers 16-33% idle power and 10-20% bandwidth, and permits smaller Cs (fact 1).

title: Vertical NEMS relays as zero-leakage DRAM access switches
idea: [Box: MIM charge | electrostatic vertical nanorelay | charge-share SA | BEOL over CMOS | Si | sacrificial release of a ~10 nm air gap] A vertically actuated nanocantilever touches the storage-node contact only while the wordline pulls it in; through an air gap the off-state leakage is essentially zero, so the cell holds charge for hours.
why: Refresh (fact 3) and voltage floor (fact 10): no subthreshold leakage and abrupt switching; contact endurance (1e12+ cycles) is the main risk.

title: 77 K cryogenic DRAM stacks with tenfold smaller capacitors
idea: [Box: small planar MIM | Si or poly-Si FET | charge-share SA | many-tier monolithic | Si | relaxed DUV] Run memory racks at liquid-nitrogen temperature where leakage falls by 1e4 or more and retention climbs to minutes; cells use 0.5-1 fF low-AR capacitors and leakier thin-film transistors, so tiers stack cheaply.
why: Capacitor wall (fact 1), refresh (fact 3) and wire energy (fact 5, Cu resistance ~6x lower): near-zero refresh, simple cells; cooling cost amortized in AI datacenters.

title: Stacked CFET four-transistor loadless latch near DRAM footprint
idea: [Box: bistable latch | complementary stacked FET (nFET over pFET) | differential SA | monolithic CFET | Si | Si/SiGe epitaxy] Build a 4T loadless cell (two pMOS access devices plus two cross-coupled nMOS held by leakage ratio) with CFET vertical stacking so the footprint approaches ~2x a 6F2 DRAM cell, with no capacitor and no refresh.
why: Refresh (fact 3), capacitor (fact 1) and destructive read (fact 8): static, non-destructive cell on a logic process; trades ~2x area for no capacitor module.

title: Two-bit cells in long lateral 3D capacitors via time-to-threshold sensing
idea: [Box: four-level charge | IGZO lateral FET | time-domain SA (bitline crossing timed by per-tier counter) | monolithic 3D | Si | ALD] Lateral capacitors in 3D DRAM can be made long (Cs ~15-20 fF) for little extra cost; spend that charge on four levels and read them by timing when the bitline crosses a single reference.
why: 3D break-even (fact 2): 2 bits per cell cuts tiers needed to beat planar from ~26 to ~13.

title: Epitaxial vertical pnpn thyristor pillars as capacitorless 4F2 cells
idea: [Box: thyristor bistable conduction | gated self-latching pnpn | current sense | monolithic, repeatable by layer transfer | Si | in-situ doped blanket epitaxy then pillar etch] Grow a blanket p+/n/p/n+ epitaxial stack so junction positions are set by deposition, etch it into pillars and wrap a gate on the p-base; the latched/blocking state is dynamic storage with large read current and no capacitor.
why: Capacitor wall (fact 1) and 3D (fact 2): no capacitor, junctions defined by epitaxy not lithography, and identical stacks can be transferred tier by tier.

title: Periphery wafer sandwiched between two array wafers, cross-face sensing
idea: [Box: 1T1C | VCT | open-bitline SA with true line above and complement below | front hybrid bond + backside bond | thinned periphery Si | hybrid bonding + nano-TSV backside contacts] Bond one array wafer to the periphery wafer's front and another to its thinned backside, so every sense amp serves an open bitline from the top array and its complement from the bottom array.
why: Periphery 49% (fact 7): one periphery layer per two arrays halves periphery cost per bit, and balanced top/bottom pairs cancel array noise.

title: CVD diamond interlayers between DRAM tiers to spread heat
idea: [Box: standard cell | any access device | any sensing | wafer stack with 1-2 um polycrystalline diamond bonding layers | Si + diamond | low-temperature diamond growth + through-diamond vias] Insert thin diamond heat spreaders (k ~1000 W/mK) between stacked dies or wafers so hotspots from logic underneath no longer raise local array temperature.
why: Retention roughly halves per ~10 C; cutting array temperature 15-20 C reduces refresh 2-4x (fact 3) and lets HBM-on-logic stacks grow taller (fact 6).

title: Anodic alumina pore lattice as mask-free 4F2 VCT array template
idea: [Box: MIM charge | coaxial IGZO VCT grown inside pores | charge-share SA | BEOL over CMOS | Si | Al anodization, no lithography for the cell lattice] Deposit Al over the bitlines, pre-texture it with a coarse ArF seed grid, and anodize to grow self-ordered hexagonal pores at ~25-40 nm pitch; ALD gate oxide, IGZO channel and storage contact coaxially inside each pore, with pore walls as the gate spacer.
why: Litho-bound capital (fact 4): the densest lattice comes from electrochemistry, with pitch set by anodization voltage; removes 2-3 EUV layers per wafer.

title: Self-organized anodic TiO2 nanotubes as both dielectric and 3D mold
idea: [Box: rutile TiO2 charge (k~80-100) | VCT | charge-share SA | BEOL | Si | Ti anodization + RuO2-templated rutile anneal] Anodize a sputtered Ti film over the landing pads into vertically aligned nanotubes nucleated on each pad, crystallize them to rutile on a RuO2 seed, and fill tube cores with the storage electrode, so the high-k dielectric grows itself in 3D with no hole lithography or plasma etch.
why: Capacitor wall (fact 1, k~70 target) and no EUV (fact 4): mold, etch and dielectric deposition collapse into one electrochemical step.

title: Block-copolymer cylinders multiply ArF guide patterns into pillar lattices
idea: [Box: MIM charge | Si VCT | charge-share SA | monolithic | Si | ArF-immersion guide trenches + PS-b-PMMA DSA, 4x density multiplication] Print coarse ~80 nm guide trenches with ArF immersion and let a block copolymer self-assemble into ~20 nm-pitch hexagonal cylinders inside them; the PMMA domains become the hard mask for VCT pillars and capacitor holes.
why: No EUV (fact 4): polymer thermodynamics multiplies density, replacing EUV on the 2-3 densest array layers at roughly a third of the litho cost per layer.

title: Mask-free interference lithography for perfectly periodic cell arrays
idea: [Box: 1T1C | VCT | standard SA | monolithic | Si | 193 nm two/three-beam immersion interference + one spacer step + low-res block mask] DRAM arrays are periodic, so expose them with mask-less two- and three-beam 193 nm immersion interference (~34 nm half-pitch per shot, ~17 nm after one spacer step) and trim array edges with a cheap low-resolution DUV block mask.
why: No EUV (fact 4): no reticle and much simpler optics; litho cost per array layer could drop to roughly a fifth of EUV.

title: Photo-electrochemical macropore etching for 150:1 silicon capacitor trenches
idea: [Box: Si trench charge | VCT | charge-share SA | capacitor-first in substrate | n-type Si | backside-illuminated anodization in HF] Seed pits with a coarse ArF or DSA pattern, then grow capacitor holes into n-Si by backside-illuminated electrochemical etching that propagates straight at AR 150+ with no plasma; line with ALD high-k and fill with TiN.
why: Capacitor wall (fact 1): AR beyond 115 without plasma etchers or EUV; wet tooling is cheap and U.S.-buildable. Sub-100 nm pore pitch is the key risk.

title: Metal-assisted chemical etching carves single-crystal VCT pillar forests
idea: [Box: MIM charge | single-crystal Si VCT | charge-share SA | monolithic | Si | DSA-patterned Pt/Au catalyst mesh + HF/H2O2 MacEtch] A perforated noble-metal mesh sinks into Si in HF/H2O2 and leaves straight, plasma-damage-free 20 nm pillars at AR >50, which become the vertical channels.
why: No EUV (fact 4) and leakage tail (fact 3): damage-free sidewalls trim the trap-assisted leakage tail, and wet tools cost far less than plasma etch.

title: Self-rolling strained nanomembrane capacitors coil into cell-size towers
idea: [Box: rolled multilayer MIM charge | VCT | charge-share SA | BEOL | Si | strained bilayer deposition + sacrificial release, coarse ArF patches only] Deposit a strained TiN/high-k/TiN stack on a sacrificial film; releasing each patch makes it roll into a multi-turn Swiss-roll tube anchored on its pad, with capacitance set by film area and number of windings.
why: Capacitor wall (fact 1): capacitance comes from deposited film area, not etched aspect ratio, so no high-AR mold and no EUV.

title: Fold one large planar array membrane into stacked layers
idea: [Box: 1T1C | planar IGZO | standard SA | accordion-folded thin-film membrane | polyimide on glass carrier | DUV-only planar process + laser lift-off + folding] Process one large array as a planar thin film with wiring continuous across fold lines, lift it off, and fold it accordion-style into 8-32 adhesive-bonded layers; interlayer connections are just the wires running around the folds.
why: Density per footprint without EUV: area becomes height, with no TSVs (fact 6) and no tier-by-tier alignment.

title: Laser-grown location-controlled silicon grains for stacked single-crystal tiers
idea: [Box: 1T1C or 2T0C | grain-boundary-free Si FET | standard SA | monolithic sequential tiers | Si | excimer laser + DUV grain-filter holes (micro-Czochralski)] On each new tier, deposit a-Si over a small DUV-patterned grain-filter hole at every transistor site and melt it with an excimer laser, so one grain grows from each hole and a single-crystal island lands exactly where each transistor goes.
why: 3D (fact 2) without EUV: near-single-crystal, low-leakage transistors on every tier at relaxed DUV pitch, with density from tier count.

title: On-chip MLCC: interleaved deposited electrodes replace deep capacitor etch
idea: [Box: multilayer interdigitated MIM | VCT | charge-share SA | monolithic | Si | blanket ALD/PVD TiN/Ru/ZrO2 multilayer + selective lateral recess] Deposit N alternating TiN and Ru electrode sheets separated by ZrO2, etch one coarse pillar per cell, then selectively recess the Ru from one sidewall and the TiN from the other so storage node and plate interleave like a ceramic MLCC.
why: Capacitor wall (fact 1): capacitance scales with deposited layer count, not aspect ratio or lithography; ~10 sheets reach >5 fF at moderate AR.

title: Mirror-bond two VCT array wafers at their common blanket plate
idea: [Box: MIM charge | 4F2 VCT | charge-share SA | face-to-face bond at the capacitor plate | Si | blanket TiN-to-TiN bond needing no fine alignment] Finish two VCT arrays with an unpatterned top plate and bond them plate-to-plate; since the shared plate is blanket, overlay can be off by microns, and the upper array's bitlines reach periphery through coarse vias at the array edge.
why: Doubles bits per footprint at the same DUV pitch with one alignment-tolerant bond, beating the ~10-20% a node shrink buys (fact 4).

title: Spacer-split pillars give two cells per 4F2 footprint
idea: [Box: two half-capacitors | split VCT with two independent channel faces | charge-share SA | monolithic | Si | ArF pillars + self-aligned spacer slot] Pattern pillars at relaxed ArF pitch, then cut each in half with a self-aligned spacer-defined slot so its two faces become separate channels gated by left and right wordlines, each tied to its own half-capacitor.
why: No EUV (fact 4): 2F2 per bit at F=20 nm (~800 nm2/bit) matches 6F2 at F=12 nm (~864 nm2/bit) without EUV.

title: One wordline metal gates IGZO tiers above and below
idea: [Box: lateral 1T1C | top- and bottom-gated IGZO pair | standard SA | monolithic 3D | Si | ALD stack, ArF hole/slit patterning only] Order each repeat as IGZO / gate oxide / wordline / gate oxide / IGZO so a single wordline gates two cell layers, removing one metal layer per pair of tiers.
why: 3D tiers (fact 2): ~30% thinner stack per bit means shallower high-AR etches for the same bit count; density comes from deposition, not lithography.

title: Plate wordlines and hole bitlines: one-mask annular 3D DRAM
idea: [Box: annular lateral capacitor | annular IGZO channel | charge-share SA | 3D-NAND-like plate stack | Si | blanket stack + one ArF hole mask + isotropic recesses] Each tier is a blanket wordline plate; one hole etch through all tiers forms vertical bitlines, and isotropic recesses carve an annular IGZO channel and ring capacitor around every hole in every tier, so a cell is (tier, hole) and mask count is independent of tier count.
why: No EUV + 3D (facts 2, 4): ArF holes at ~80 nm pitch x 100 tiers give ~64 nm2 per bit, ~13x denser than 6F2 at 12 nm; small ring Cs is the risk.

title: Keep the SiGe layers: superlattice wells become floating-body storage
idea: [Box: holes in a SiGe quantum well | lateral Si nanosheet FET | current sense | monolithic Si/SiGe superlattice | Si | epitaxy-defined layers, ArF slits] Normally the SiGe in a 3D-DRAM superlattice is sacrificial; instead grade each sheet as Si channel / thin SiGe well / Si so the valence-band offset traps holes as a capacitorless storage node under each lateral gate.
why: 3D blockers (fact 2): no lateral capacitor, ~3x shorter cell; all critical dimensions set by epitaxy thickness.

title: Overlay-free crossbar cells from bonding two orthogonal line wafers
idea: [Box: MIM charge | two-terminal threshold selector (OTS/NbO2) | pulsed charge-share sensing | face-to-face bond of two line-grating wafers | Si | ArF SAQP gratings on each wafer] Wafer A carries bitline gratings capped with capacitor films, wafer B carries orthogonal wordline gratings capped with selector film; bonding them makes every crossing a 1S1C cell, and any overlay error only shifts the whole grid.
why: No EUV (fact 4): lines are the easiest ArF pattern and cells need no alignment, giving 4F2 at F~20 nm; selector leakage limits retention.

title: Capacitor walls instead of pillars: line gratings segmented by self-aligned cuts
idea: [Box: MIM on both wall faces | VCT | charge-share SA | monolithic | Si | ArF SADP line gratings + cuts self-aligned to wordlines] Form storage electrodes as continuous tall oxide-core walls, far stiffer than isolated pillars so AR 120+ does not lean, coat both faces, then segment each wall into per-cell plates with cuts self-aligned to the wordlines.
why: Capacitor wall (fact 1, AR ~115 target): line/space patterns suit ArF, and the extra height delivers more charge without EUV.

title: Two-deck capacitor molds joined like 3D NAND channel decks
idea: [Box: MIM | VCT | charge-share SA | monolithic | Si | two sequential 50:1 mold decks + self-aligned conductive inter-deck plug] Etch the capacitor mold as two stacked 50:1 decks joined by a self-aligned plug, building electrodes in each, for ~100:1 effective height from ArF-resolvable holes and production-proven etches.
why: Capacitor wall (fact 1): ~100-115 effective AR without new etch physics or EUV.

title: Area-selective ALD grows landing pads only on contacts
idea: [Box: MIM | VCT | standard SA | monolithic | Si | inhibitor-based area-selective ALD of Ru on TiN, not on SiO2] Replace the overlay-critical landing-pad and storage-contact lithography with bottom-up growth: inhibitor molecules passivate the dielectric, and Ru nucleates only on exposed contacts, self-limiting into mushroom pads.
why: No EUV (fact 4): removes 1-2 critical layers and their overlay budget, because each pad is self-aligned to its contact.

title: Display fabs build IGZO memory tiers on Gen-8.5 glass panels
idea: [Box: 2T0C gain charge | IGZO TFT | current sense | many-tier panel-level stack | 2.2 x 2.5 m glass | i-line/ArF dry steppers in existing LCD/OLED fabs] Use idle display-fab capacity to build IGZO gain-cell arrays at ~0.5 um F on huge glass panels, stack 8-16 tiers, and dice them into CXL capacity-tier memory modules.
why: Capital intensity and supply: at 8F2, F=0.5 um gives ~60 GB/m2 per tier, ~340 GB per panel tier; glass costs ~100x less per m2 than processed Si, with no EUV.

title: Single-exposure ArF array, density made up by tier count
idea: [Box: lateral 1T1C | IGZO | standard SA | monolithic 3D | Si | single-exposure ArF immersion only (>=38 nm half-pitch), no multipatterning] Freeze lateral pitch at what one ArF immersion exposure can print and make tier count the only scaling knob, co-designing a wide-pitch cell (longer lateral capacitor, relaxed contacts) so mask count stays almost flat from 32 to 200 tiers.
why: Litho-bound capital (fact 4): no EUV and no SAQP, so depreciation share falls as bits grow through cheap deposition/etch cycles.

title: Array tiers on reclaimed or glass carriers, bonded to foundry periphery
idea: [Box: IGZO 1T1C/2T0C tiers | IGZO | standard SA | CMOS-bonded-array hybrid bond | reclaimed Si or glass carrier | DUV-only; periphery from U.S. 22-28 nm foundries] BEOL IGZO array tiers do not need single-crystal Si, so build them on cheap reclaimed or glass carrier wafers and hybrid-bond them to periphery wafers bought from existing U.S. 22-28 nm DUV foundries.
why: Scarce resources (prime CZ wafers depend on Spruce Pine quartz crucibles) and U.S. manufacturability: about half the prime-wafer demand per bit, and no EUV on either wafer.

title: Convert 3D NAND lines into 3D DRAM lines sharing tool sets
idea: [Box: plate-stack 3D DRAM | IGZO or poly-Si | CMOS-under-array | 3D-NAND-style stacking | Si | existing NAND high-AR etch, replacement-gate and staircase tools] Design the 3D DRAM flow around 3D NAND tool recipes and contract NAND makers' underused EUV-free lines, swinging capacity between NAND and DRAM as prices move.
why: Capital and time (fact 4): skips the 3-5 year, $15B+ greenfield fab; NAND lines already own the high-AR etch and deposition tools, and supply can flex quarterly.
